Radboudumc Radiology Service | 08 Jan 2025
Study: Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate
Indication: Follow-up after a previously positive biopsy. Current prostate-specific antigen stands at 28.3.

Findings: The gland occupies a total volume of 70.0 mL. A discrete abnormality localizes to the left peripheral zone, spanning the base through mid-gland, measuring roughly 28 mm longest diameter. T2 sequences highlight pronounced hypointensity within this focus. Diffusion-weighted techniques demonstrate marked restriction, mirrored by low apparent diffusion coefficient values. Post-contrast phases show prompt, localized enhancement compared to adjacent tissue. Seminal vesicles appear normal and symmetrical. Pelvic lymph nodes show no suspicious morphology, and capsular integrity remains intact without extracapsular spread.

Impression: Left peripheral zone mass scoring PI-RADS 5. Calculated PSA density registers 0.4. Estimated csPCa probability computes to 0.8709831.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: An April 2024 PSA draw returned 23.1 ng/mL, continuing the rising trend established since the initial biopsy confirmed a Positive result earlier in the calendar year. Clinical tracking focused on lower urinary tract symptom progression and overall health status.

Discussion centered on the pathological features and general prognosis. Scheduled laboratory assessments and symptom tracking continued.
